meta.title: The Creamery | Beaver UT — Knighton Architecture

blocks.html:
The Creamery | Beaver UT

Each of our projects at Knighton Architecture has a story that matters to the business owner, so it matters to us. A few years ago, the iconic cheese plant in Beaver was in need of a refresh. The local managers had a vision of expanding the small cheese store attached to the plant, and the Dairy Farmers of America (DFA) leadership saw the potential to create a unique experience that brings the farm directly to the table.

What was once a small building to the side of a dairy processing plant, became a beautiful new building with more customers than anyone could have imagined. The new store features expanded retail space, a cafe, and an interactive, educational dairy experience space. It’s had a massive positive impact on the local community as well as the family farmers represented by Dairy Farmers of America, telling their story of bringing fresh dairy products from farm to table. This is only one illustration of how our process works – which begins with an idea and ends with positive impacts on communities.

Patey Aviation Park

Nestled within the Spanish Fork Airport, this private hangar community caters to aviation enthusiasts with a design that blends sleek, modern forms with nods to aviation heritage.

The development’s layout prioritizes accessibility, with direct taxiway access and integrated services for convenience. This hangar community seamlessly blends utility and lifestyle, creating a functional, inspiring space for aviation lovers.

At the heart of the development is the Flight Base Operations (FBO) building, offering panoramic views of the runway and Wasatch Mountains. It features a restaurant, lounge, and office spaces, blending elegance with functionality.

Hangars offer access to a shared amenity space with a lounge, kitchenette, and restroom, fostering a sense of community. Select hangars include private amenity spaces for added exclusivity.

With hangars now available for purchase, this project is quickly becoming a landmark of aviation excellence.

meta.title: Pax Station Apartments — Knighton Architecture

blocks.html:
Pax Station Apartments | Salt Lake City UT

Located next to the Ballpark TRAX Station in Salt Lake City, Pax Station Apartments transforms a former infill junkyard site into a vibrant, transit-oriented community. Designed to address the city’s growing need for affordable housing, the project will activate an underutilized transit stop and reimagine a narrow street into a welcoming pedestrian corridor.

The development features a thoughtful mix of micro-units—two-thirds micro-studios and one-third micro one-bedrooms—designed to maximize efficiency and livability. Residents will enjoy shared amenities including a rooftop deck with sweeping views of the Wasatch Mountains and a central elevated courtyard above the parking garage, framed by a U-shaped floor plan that ensures abundant natural light in every home.

This project has been made possible through a strong and collaborative team effort. Capital Real Estate Advisors and Redstone Residential lead the development partnership, with Bonneville Construction serving as General Contractor. From pre-construction through budget management, the team has worked seamlessly to deliver an impactful project that remains on budget. With permits approved, construction is set to begin in Fall 2025.

blocks.addr: 201 Paxton Avenue, Salt Lake City, UT, 84101

Forge Jewelry Works | Provo UT

Breathing new life into a historic building with strong architectural character, the Forge Jewelry Works headquarters underwent a full interior renovation and exterior transformation. The result is a vibrant home for a business that celebrates craftsmanship—where skilled jewelsmiths create custom pieces in full view of their clients.

meta.title: Payson Passive House | Payson UT — Knighton Architecture

blocks.html:
Payson Passive House

Introducing our first custom home in Payson, Utah, designed to achieve Passive House certification. This modern two-story residence exemplifies sustainable living through innovative passive heating and cooling strategies, significantly reducing energy consumption while ensuring year-round comfort.

The home features a hyper-insulated building envelope, maintaining optimal indoor temperatures and providing exceptional air quality. Its efficient layout maximizes space and functionality, highlighted by a unique cantilever design that doubles as a carport, optimizing the use of the site.

Built to last, this home not only prioritizes energy efficiency but also offers a comfortable and healthy living environment, setting a new standard for sustainable residential design.

The Madison + The Winston

In 2016, our team played a key role in redesigning the interior of the historic Madison Building on Center Street in downtown Provo. Once home to a cowboy bar on the upper floors and a nightclub on the ground floor, the building was reimagined by the owner, Steven Bond of Capital Advisors Real Estate. The upper floors were transformed into a real estate brokerage office, while the ground floor became a dry bar comedy venue.

A few years later, the adjacent building, renamed “The Winston,” became available. Partnering again with Steven Bond, we undertook a comprehensive renovation, adding a new upper floor and a rear expansion to accommodate creative office spaces and a dance hall. This project has become a dynamic addition to downtown Provo, now serving as the headquarters for Angel Studios and enhancing the area’s vitality.

meta.title: Halvorsen Candy Bomber Museum | Spanish Fork UT — Knighton Architecture

blocks.html:
Halvorsen ‘Candy Bomber’ Museum and Education Center

Celebrating the legacy of Gail Halvorsen, "The Candy Bomber," this museum and STEM education center combines history, innovation, and timeless design. The building’s Art Deco-inspired architecture pays homage to the era of the Berlin Airlift, with streamlined forms, geometric detailing, and a sense of forward momentum that reflects Halvorsen’s humanitarian mission and the transformative power of aviation. Iconic materials of polished stone, metallic accents, and decorative glass enhance the building’s sense of elegance and historical resonance.

The interior balances form and function, with museum galleries that chronicle Halvorsen’s life and the Berlin Airlift, alongside vibrant STEM labs where visitors can engage with hands-on activities exploring the principles of flight and engineering. High ceilings, large windows, and intricate detailing create spaces that are both inspiring and welcoming. Outdoor areas, such as a garden or sculpture court, extend the experience, offering places for reflection and gathering. The design beautifully merges the inspiration of Halvorsen’s story with the optimism and innovation of the Art Deco era.

team.name: Jeff Knighton AIA NCARB | Founder + Principal Architect

meta.title: Jeff Knighton AIA NCARB | Founder + Principal Architect — Knighton Architecture

blocks.html:
Jeff Knighton AIA NCARB | Founder + Principal Architect

Raised in Provo Utah, Jeff had the desire to draw and create at a young age, and decided as a kid that he wanted to become an architect. In high school he took an advanced architectural drafting course, where he designed his first project – a new custom home for his parents – and then helped to build it the following summer.

The experience of taking something imagined in the mind and turning it into a built reality that enhanced someone else’s life was life-changing and set the hook for Jeff. He went on to study Urban Planning at Brigham Young University, and then pursued a master’s degree in Architecture at the University of Oregon, also earning a graduate certificate in Ecological Design. After studying and working in the Northwest for several years, he moved back to Utah to live closer to family and set out to create his own architectural practice that focused on creative and meaningful projects, strong client relationships, and a collaborative family-like environment.

He is a father of five busy kids, and a colon cancer survivor (diagnosed the same year he started his own business). He is passionate about getting outside and exploring the natural world with his family. He also loves to play his guitar and dreams of writing and recording his own music.

meta.title: Knighton Before Christmas: A Gingerbread-Building Charity Event Supporting HomeAid Utah — Knighton Architecture

blocks.html:
Knighton Architecture, alongside our partners and community, proudly hosted The Knighton Before Christmas, a festive gingerbread-building charity event in support of HomeAid Utah. Designed to bring together families, colleagues, and friends, the evening blended creativity, connection, and purpose—raising awareness and funds for individuals and families experiencing homelessness in our community.

Event Inspiration

Rooted in the spirit of the holiday season, the event was created as a meaningful way to celebrate creativity while giving back. Gingerbread building served as the centerpiece activity, encouraging friendly competition, teamwork, and imagination across all ages. The event reflected Knighton Architecture’s belief that design—at any scale—has the power to bring people together.

Community, Creativity, and Giving

Participants gathered to design and construct gingerbread creations while enjoying food, hot chocolate, and a welcoming atmosphere. The gingerbread competition offered an engaging way to support HomeAid Utah, with entry fees donated directly to the organization. Additional opportunities to contribute throughout the evening further strengthened the collective impact of the event.

Competition and Celebration

The gingerbread competition showcased impressive creativity and craftsmanship, with competitors recognized through a variety of curated prizes. The energy of the evening was fueled not only by the competition itself, but by shared laughter, collaboration, and the joy of celebrating the season together.

Collaboration and Support

The success of The Knighton Before Christmas was made possible through the generosity of participants, donors, and supporters who contributed prizes, time, and resources. Their involvement helped transform a festive gathering into a meaningful charitable effort with lasting impact.

A Commitment to Community

Events like this reflect Knighton Architecture’s ongoing commitment to community engagement and social responsibility. By supporting organizations like HomeAid Utah, we aim to extend our impact beyond the built environment and contribute to initiatives that strengthen and uplift our region.

We are grateful to everyone who joined us, competed, donated, and helped make The Knighton Before Christmas a memorable and impactful event. We look forward to continuing to create opportunities where design, community, and purpose come together.

The Utah Valley Parade of Homes is a platform for celebrating design innovation in the region, and Valley View stands as an example of how thoughtful architecture can enrich daily life. At Knighton Architecture, we are proud to see this home realized and look forward to continuing to design spaces that inspire and endure.

posts.title: Restoring the Fifth Ward Chapel: Reviving a Salt Lake City Landmark
posts.excerpt: Knighton Architecture is honored to partner with Skylar Baird on the restoration of the historic Fifth Ward Chapel in Salt Lake City. Originally built in 1910 and recognized as both a National Register and Salt Lake City Landmark, the chapel is being returned to its original architectural form after decades of change and a recent partial demolition. Our team has restored the design to reflect its authentic character, and we look forward to seeing this landmark continue its new life as a space for community renewal.

meta.title: Restoring the Fifth Ward Chapel: Reviving a Salt Lake City Landmark — Knighton Architecture
meta.description: Knighton Architecture is honored to partner with Skylar Baird on the restoration of the historic  Fifth Ward Chapel  in Salt Lake City. Originally built in 1910 and recognized as both a National Register and Salt Lake City Landmark, the chapel is being returned to its original architectural form after decades of change and a recent partial demolition. Our team has restored the design to reflect its authentic character, and we look forward to seeing this landmark continue its new life as a space for community renewal.

blocks.html: The Fifth Ward Chapel, also known as the Fifth Ward Meetinghouse, has stood at 740 South 300 West in Salt Lake City, Utah since 1910. Designed by the respected architectural firm Cannon & Fetzer, the chapel is an important example of Gothic Revival and Tudor Revival architecture and has long been recognized as a landmark of the city’s cultural and architectural heritage.

For more than six decades, the building served as a meetinghouse for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. After being sold in the 1970s, the chapel found new life in many forms, including as a music venue, a Buddhist temple, and a community arts center. In recognition of its historic and architectural significance, the Fifth Ward Chapel was added to the National Register of Historic Places and designated a Salt Lake City Landmark in 1978.

In recent years, the chapel faced serious challenges. Following an unauthorized partial demolition in 2024, concerns grew about the loss of one of Salt Lake City’s most treasured historic structures. Fortunately, new ownership and a renewed commitment to preservation have given the building a second chance.

Knighton Architecture is honored to be leading the architectural restoration of the Fifth Ward Chapel. Our team has carefully studied the building’s history and original design, restoring the plans to reflect the chapel’s authentic 1910 appearance. This approach ensures that the structure will not only regain its historic character but also stand as a lasting example of preservation and adaptive reuse in Salt Lake City.

As the project progresses, the chapel will once again serve the community, providing space for renewal and connection while honoring its historic roots. At Knighton Architecture, we are proud to contribute our expertise in historic preservation and architectural restoration in Utah, and we look forward to seeing the continued progress of this important project.

Retail & Restaurants

Allow us to assist in conveying your brand narrative crafting the customer experience you envision. We engage with our retail and restaurant clients to facilitate the creation of distinctive experiences for their customers, ensuring they are both memorable and meaningful.

Aviation

Our recent work with Patey Aviation Park in Spanish Fork, Utah, has solidified our expertise in private aviation design, subsequently opening avenues for additional opportunities in other aviation projects.

Custom Residences

We offer high-level custom design services for clients seeking a personalized and experience-driven design for their personal residence or vacation home.

Office & Workplace

We collaborate with clients to create innovative, adaptable work environments tailored to individual and organizational needs.

Preservation & Adaptive Re-Use

Having worked in several historic buildings, we can bring new life to an existing or otherwise tired structure or space by finding creative solutions despite fixed constraints.

Passive House & High-Performance

With a certified Passive House designer on our team, we can provide high-performance design and energy modeling for our clients and assist those interested in pursuing PHIUS certification.

Interior Design

We provide integrated interior design services alongside our architecture or as standalone options tailored to clients' needs.

Landscape Design

We can provide integrated in-house landscape design services for our residential design projects.

STEP 1 | Project Discovery

Before we start designing, we gather the information needed to begin the project. We meet with you to understand your needs, expectations, end goals, budgets, and any constraints you might have. We also study local zoning codes and regulations. If circumstances permit, we’d love to visit the site to help us understand the opportunities and challenges of your unique location.

STEP 2 | Concept Design

Once we understand the ideas and needs behind the project, we start with early conceptual design. We share ideas, explore possibilities, and give you a preview of what the project could ultimately look like. If the project is feasible and meets your needs, we will move to the next phase. Occasionally, it becomes clear that a project does not fit the site, or vice versa. In those instances, we will collaboratively tweak the design until you feel ready to proceed to the next phase.

STEP 3 | Construction Documents

This is where the real fun (and work) starts. We delve into the details of the design and carefully address all the complex elements that come together to bring the project to life. We offer digital 3D renderings and virtual walkthroughs to help you visualize and imagine what the project will look like when it's completed. Our team collaborates with various professional engineers who provide the technical specifications necessary to ensure the project is buildable. Additionally, we prepare the drawings and documents for city approval and guide you through that process.

STEP 4 | Construction Administration

At this point, your project truly comes to life. We provide support throughout construction to advocate for the owner, working closely with the contractor to coordinate and resolve any issues that arise during the building process. Our goal is to ensure that the project unfolds according to the plans. We remain engaged and by your side until the project is ready for you to move in.

EXPLORE

The initial step in each project involves identifying the design problem. This includes a comprehensive understanding of the purpose, the site, the context, the future users, and the budget.

Similarly, at our firm, we are committed to actively learning and exploring innovative approaches to assist our clients, to engage with emerging markets, and to adopt new technologies. We strive to maintain a continual understanding of the complex and dynamic world that surrounds us.

+

CREATE

Once the design problem is identified, the design process begins with the creation of various design concepts. These concepts are subjected to testing and review through an iterative process, leading to the selection and preparation of the final design for construction.

Our team fosters a culture of collaboration and creativity, ensuring that the best ideas win.

+

ELEVATE

Ultimately, the goal of every design is for that design idea to become a real place that makes a real impact in the world for good. By staying engaged with our clients through the construction process, we help the contractor to ensure the client's vision is achieved.

Our end goal as a team is to make a positive impact in the world through thoughtfully designed and constructed improvements that elevate the community and the world at large.

HOW WE APPROACH PRICING/FEES

Pricing for professional design services can be difficult to predict due to the numerous variables inherent to each project. The descriptions below provide a framework for how we typically approach our fee structures. However, we recommend reaching out and scheduling an initial design consultation so we can review the details together, allowing us to provide a detailed fee proposal for your unique project.

Commercial | Multi-Family | Institutional

Typically 3%–7% of Expected Construction Costs

Cost Contributing Factors:

  • Additional engineering services. Civil, Structural, MEP Engineering, Landscape and/or Interior Design.
  • Project size, complexity and timeframe

*Proposals are prepared individually per project

Custom Residential

Typically $3–$7* per sq ft of Livable Space

Cost Contributing Factors:

  • Additional engineering services. Civil, Structural, MEP Engineering, Landscape and/or Interior Design.
  • Required additional approvals such as HOA Design Review, etc.

*Proposals are prepared individually per project

Master-planning & Site Planning

Typically $1K–$2K per acre of Developable Land

Cost Contributing Factors:

  • Additional engineering services. Civil, Structural, MEP Engineering, Landscape and/or Interior Design.
  • Required additional approvals

*Proposals are prepared individually per project
